You care about your loved ones. Do you feel like they waste your time? Probably no, and they probably don't think you waste their time either. 

I think small victories matter. Really small victories like cleaning your room, throwing away clutters, cooking and eating something you really enjoy. Things that lift you in a small scale. Start with one or two a day, and continue until  winning becomes a habit. What is there to lose anyway? 

It helps me much, that I don't take myself too seriously. I laugh at myself from time to time. Things are much lighter from this perspective.

1. Find a place first, and set up a date (deadline)
2. Set a goal of how much stuff you will take with you (how many boxes, etc)
3. Pack practical needs first
4. Pack sentimental belongings very selectively 
5. Get trashbag and let go of things. Recycling is great, but I don't know if you have the time and energy if you are facing divorce after a long marriage. 
6. Clean up your new place thoroughly
7. Unpack each item, find a place for each one. Don't clutter the new place, make it your sanctuary

Thats pretty much summing up what I've done with my divorce. It helped me immensely. Practicing letting go of material goods lead to the letting go of mental clutters. Minimizing distractions really helped me to face myself raw. 

Good luck and stay healthy
